Save planning/criterion changes before collecting and publishing results. Initial PX2 publication cannot contain pass/fail V. Unavailable observations do not claim evaluation and are exempt from this ordering rule. This establishes recorded ordering between a plan and its verdict; it cannot independently attest when a person actually inspected an image.

A done task must reopen when it or its relevant dependency closure changes. PX2 closure does not traverse through P: an unrelated intake choice or project display name does not reopen an accepted sample. Link actual semantic dependencies through its input/output contracts, choices, criteria, sources and decisions. Changing one of those dependencies requires reopening and superseding stale E/V before new evaluation. History remains available for cold resumption.

The optional [selected-asset preparation adapter](asset-preparation.md) authors the
existing candidate/sample records from exact reviewed PLAR artifacts and retains
input bytes. Its explicit versioned report-X metadata binding also checks current
PLAR identity before new job preparation/dispatch; it does not add record fields or
relabel an expert candidate interpretation as owner-approved production.

## Operational boundaries

The optional [candidate/family review adapter](candidate-review.md) retains explicit
observations through existing X/E/V, derives exact evidence scope and connects
nomination/completion with recoverable publication. It adds no registry fields;
prepared inspection packets retain their existing coverage contract.

The optional [connected production-plan adapter](production-plan.md) authors
family/stage wiring from reviewed JSON and binds exact accepted upstream inputs
before preparing a staged request. It uses existing T/F/Q/X and PLAR metadata;
contracts, adoption, provider execution and acceptance keep their existing meaning.

Use `intake`, `decode`, `encode`, `validate`, `commit`, `workflow`, `ready`, `context` and `impact` through the selected runner; MCP adds `pixl_intake` and `pixl_workflow`. `context` retains PX2 format and complete references. Mutable state and evidence live in the art project, outside installed resources. Generic encode/commit can author the declared records; they do not perform inspection or grant approval.

This version supplies the local intake/sample lifecycle. The original platform prepare/job tools remain stateless local operations. Real PixelLab execution, actual visual judgments, destination-engine verification and model performance require their own observed evidence.

## Durable provider jobs (registry 2.1.0 extension)

J opts into durable history by supplying `jr` (current journal report X), `op` (nonempty distinct F outputs) and `xs` (all imported X candidates in event order, initially empty). J.xs preserves typed dependency closure for focused retrieval; these are not task nominations. Existing J without these fields retains its earlier semantics. A published legacy J cannot acquire this extension, and a durable J cannot shed it. Older PX2 readers reject these additional fields explicitly. PX1 schema and semantics are unchanged.

The retained journal uses the version-1 closed JSON contract in [provider-recovery.md](provider-recovery.md). J.tk/tl/ah/si/ri/op must exactly project its task/tool/intent hash/state/remote identity/outputs. J.ev retains ordered local E receipts for every snapshot, starting with prepared intent and adding one snapshot per event. Each non-superseded local passing E binds exactly its immutable journal X and shares its path/hash. The last receipt binds J.jr. Such a pass establishes retention and local consistency; it is not remote, mechanical, visual or engine acceptance.

Generic rooted validation replays the journal and every prefix, verifies local bytes and candidate bindings, and rejects invented projections. Publication requires a saved unchanged production plan before new prepared intent, one event per subsequent commit, immutable intent, immutable retained X/E, and unchanged imported candidates. No initial-state job can invent earlier submission history. Preparation and dispatch require satisfied task activation prerequisites and an open/active task. Another nonterminal durable attempt for an overlapping output, or an unjournaled nonterminal job for the task, blocks new preparation/dispatch.

The local dispatch claim publishes `unknown` before returning the request to its host. It does not contact a service. Unknown work must be reconciled rather than resubmitted. Caller-supplied observations retain the returned identity and evidence; accepted states require an ID, which cannot change once recorded. Failed and succeeded are terminal except that success may import new candidates. Completion never follows from provider success: imported candidates still require their declared V criteria.

Changed request context blocks dispatch but does not erase submitted history or prevent recording observations. Recovery reports list drift and next actions. Imports bind copied local bytes and the original output plan; a changed output plan must be reconciled before import. All operations use expected-hash publication. Unreferenced immutable blobs may remain after a failed commit; state.px is the sole publication authority. Local coordination cannot guarantee exactly-once remote execution or prevent a host from bypassing the procedure.

## Family production and delivery (registry 2.2.0 extension)

An optional F.bs names the exact X baseline for production or delivery. It is a semantic dependency, unlike the workflow-only T.ip. The baseline must belong to another sample task in the same project; its X is also listed in the consuming task's ip, and its task is a direct dp prerequisite. Open plans may preserve an unaccepted or replaced baseline. Activation/completion requires that exact sample still nominated and its task done. A sample's passing evidence does not automatically accept a family member.

F.mb and F.ds together opt a report-kind output of a delivery task into the family operation and require bs. mb is a nonempty distinct ordered list of planned F members; ds is a nonempty distinct list of same-project I destination choices. Members cannot be the family output itself or another family output. They are the baseline's sample output or same-project production outputs sharing that exact bs. All member tasks are direct delivery prerequisites. A family declares at least one continuity Q, with project-specific mode/conditions; engine Q is declared when applicable. All destination choices must be confirmed for delivery activation/completion. Missing/unavailable engine acceptance remains separately represented through Q/V.

A family manifest X has xs: baseline X first, then one selected X per member in the saved order (the baseline may also be a delivered member). xs belongs only to family report candidates and is required on every candidate of a family output. These references bind collective acceptance to the actual baseline, selected member identities, their plans/contracts and the destination/criteria scope. Merely listing siblings in T.ip does not supply this semantic proof.

The [family delivery manifest contract](family-delivery.md) governs immutable copied files, saved-plan publication, historical membership and current acceptance. Existing family F cannot shed bs/mb/ds, and existing X cannot acquire fabricated snapshot history. Once published, a manifest X and its baseline/member X records are immutable; revisions add new candidate IDs. Changes to underlying contracts/requirements still require the existing supersession/reopening procedure.

`family` / `pixl_family` reports baseline eligibility, member and collective acceptance, destination choices, pending provider attempts, saved snapshots and drift. `family-snapshot` / `pixl_family_snapshot` retains selected member bytes and publishes an unaccepted report candidate. It requires an open/active family task, the accepted baseline and all selected members on done tasks, no pending attempts for involved tasks, and the unchanged previously saved family plan. Snapshotting local files is allowed while destination/adoption/collective acceptance remains unresolved; it does not activate, nominate, evaluate or complete the delivery task. Actual artistic continuity and target-engine readiness require their own inspection and evidence.

PLAR-bound continuation uses the [allocation/revision contract](asset-preparation.md#allocation-and-revised-work). Pending attempts for the same explicitly tagged asset exclude new jobs even under different task/output IDs. New task activation/completion checks the current selection and selected generation; retained historical validation is unchanged.

1	# Request and criteria handoff
2	
3	Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.
4	
5	## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract
6	
7	Use the focused authoring context described in [family delivery](family-delivery.md)
8	to locate current records before exploring histories. Keep a proposal's shared
9	source index once and reference its entries from individual clauses; preserve each
10	clause's authority, scope and exact locator. Do not duplicate whole reports in
11	every criterion, abbreviate literal checks into a group summary, or treat the
12	index's source class as requirement authority. Read the original source text for
13	the comparison; retrieve a complete record/history only where it bears on the
14	decision. Exact connected review remains the handoff for adoption.
15	
16	For a connected family/stage plan, use the adapter's returned `request_review`
17	arguments and retain that exact report as described in
18	[the connected handoff](#connected-family-and-stage-handoff). It supplies the saved
19	criteria and request evidence without manually rebuilding a candidate packet.
20	
21	For other contracts, save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:
22	
23	- `version`: 1.
24	- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Numbered locators refer to that individual file, never a concatenated multi-file terminal display. The caller verifies the cited content at those locators. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
25	- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
26	- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
27	- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
28	- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.
29	
30	Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.
31	
32	Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.
33	
34	Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.
35	
36	### Measured facts in creative requests
37	
38	Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.
39	
40	Keep centering calculations in one coordinate convention. For a half-open box
41	`[left, top, right, bottom]`, its centre in pixel-edge coordinates is
42	`((left + right) / 2, (top + bottom) / 2)` and the canvas centre is `(width / 2, height / 2)`.
43	A centroid computed from zero-based pixel indices needs `+0.5` per axis to use those
44	same edge coordinates. A margin imbalance, box-centre offset and mass-centroid offset
45	are different quantities; retain the actual calculation before calling an asset centred.
46	
47	The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.
48	
49	## Resolve source evidence for the comparison
50	
51	For candidate plans used by selected-asset preparation, call `pixl_request_review`
52	with the packet path and selected `asset_id` (CLI `request-review PACKET --asset ID
53	--root PROJECT`). It reads the exact request/criteria identities, returns cited text
54	with file-local bounds, and includes the current production continuation. It reports
55	invalid/unresolved locators and changed sources. A resolved excerpt is evidence for
56	the caller to interpret, not a consistency verdict. Retain this report with the review.
57	
58	Copy a host-spilled tool report as exact bytes before inspecting or formatting it.
59	These tool reports are UTF-8 JSON: use an explicit UTF-8 decoder (for example,
60	`Path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`), not the Windows process default. If saving a
61	formatted copy, compare its parsed value with the raw report before returning its
62	path/hash. A new file hash alone cannot detect text changed by a wrong decoder.
63	Keep the raw report alongside any formatted copy.
64	
65	When the connection is already discovered, bind `request.provider` and
66	`request.connection: {path, sha256}` to its exact artifact. Preparation compares that
67	reviewed connection with the supplied one; host credentials stay outside the artifact.
68	
69	Use `lines: [first,last]` on a criterion's source pointer when citing text; retain
70	`locator` as a human-readable label. Preparation validates explicit bounds before
71	saving new work. Numbered prose in older plans remains readable and receives
72	locator diagnostics. For non-text references inspect the actual image/animation;
73	for named sections resolve the location through the existing source tool. Do not
74	mark a locator verified merely because its claimed wording appears elsewhere.
75	
76	The optional criterion `authority` uses PLAR's requirement/proposal/observation/unknown
77	labels. Keep its basis and scope explicit. This label is an assertion to compare,
78	not an automatic grant of owner authority.
79	
80	## Caller: inspect before adopting
81	
82	### Connected family and stage handoff
83	
84	`pixl_production_plan` and `pixl_stage_prepare` return `request_review` arguments
85	for this same review tool. Pass that object to `pixl_request_review`; `packet`
86	names the store's `state.px`, `plan` names its exact connected-plan X, and `job`
87	is present after preparation. Existing plans can use those IDs directly. The
88	report includes every authored member and collective criterion with its full Q
89	ID, record hash, literal check and source evidence. Authority starts unclassified:
90	source presence or a validator pass cannot assign it. Changed plan/source/PLAR
91	identities remain visible so historical interpretation can be reviewed without
92	making an obsolete request current.
93	
94	The specialist returns this report's path/hash, explicit choices and any proposed
95	corrections. The caller reads the original evidence and records one
96	`criterion_comparisons` entry for **each** returned ID, including collective rules:
97	
98	```json
99	{
100	  "review_scope_sha256": "REPORT_REVIEW_SCOPE_HASH",
101	  "criterion_comparisons": [{
102	    "criterion": "EXACT_Q_ID",

# Request and criteria handoff

Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.

## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract

Use the focused authoring context described in [family delivery](family-delivery.md)
to locate current records before exploring histories. Keep a proposal's shared
source index once and reference its entries from individual clauses; preserve each
clause's authority, scope and exact locator. Do not duplicate whole reports in
every criterion, abbreviate literal checks into a group summary, or treat the
index's source class as requirement authority. Read the original source text for
the comparison; retrieve a complete record/history only where it bears on the
decision. Exact connected review remains the handoff for adoption.

For a connected family/stage plan, use the adapter's returned `request_review`
arguments and retain that exact report as described in
[the connected handoff](#connected-family-and-stage-handoff). It supplies the saved
criteria and request evidence without manually rebuilding a candidate packet.

For other contracts, save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:

- `version`: 1.
- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Numbered locators refer to that individual file, never a concatenated multi-file terminal display. The caller verifies the cited content at those locators. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.

Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.

Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.

Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.

### Measured facts in creative requests

Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.

Keep centering calculations in one coordinate convention. For a half-open box
`[left, top, right, bottom]`, its centre in pixel-edge coordinates is
`((left + right) / 2, (top + bottom) / 2)` and the canvas centre is `(width / 2, height / 2)`.
A centroid computed from zero-based pixel indices needs `+0.5` per axis to use those
same edge coordinates. A margin imbalance, box-centre offset and mass-centroid offset
are different quantities; retain the actual calculation before calling an asset centred.

The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.

formatted copy, compare its parsed value with the raw report before returning its

# Exact request and criterion review evidence

`request-review PACKET --root ROOT [--asset ID] [--plar PATH]` and
`pixl_request_review({packet, asset_id?, path?})` expose the same read-only report.
They resolve the existing version-1 request-review packet and candidate-plan JSON.
They do not write a caller review, classify semantic consistency, or authorize a
provider call. The [skill procedure](../plugins/pixl/skills/pixl/references/request-review.md)
assigns the actual comparison to the calling agent.

Saved packet, candidate-plan and caller-comparison versions follow the
[adapter compatibility policy](adapter-compatibility.md). Legacy absent comparison
versions remain distinct from unsupported explicit versions.

Connected authoring additionally returns ready arguments for this same operation:
`pixl_request_review({packet: STATE_PATH, plan: PLAN_ID, job?: JOB_ID,
comparison?: CALLER_JSON})`. The CLI equivalents are `--plan`, `--job` and
`--comparison`. This route reads all member and collective criteria from the bound
plan, resolves their sources and includes the optional job's actual request and
current blockers. It leaves authority unclassified for the caller to determine.
The optional comparison checks exact identity and coverage, not semantic agreement.
See [connected-plan review](production-plan.md#exact-criteria-handoff) for its scope
fingerprint, drift handling and comparison fields. Existing candidate packets keep
their previous semantics.

The report verifies request/criteria byte hashes and returns their exact arguments,
criterion checks, stated bases/authority/scopes, candidate controls and packet choices.
All packet source identities are checked, including references not cited by criteria.
An optional request.connection path/hash binds the exact connection artifact, and
request.provider binds its provider name. Reports verify the artifact identity; new
preparation requires the supplied connection to equal the reviewed one. Existing
packets without these optional assertions keep their previous preparation contract.
Criterion source references produce file-local excerpts or explicit diagnostics for
changed, unavailable, binary, invalid, unresolved or excessively broad locations.
`consistent` remains null and `caller_comparison` remains unperformed. A valid source
range does not show that the requirement entails the authored rejection condition.

Candidate criteria may add `authority` (requirement, proposal, observation, unknown).
A text source pointer may add `lines: [first,last]`, with one-based inclusive integer
bounds, alongside its existing path/locator. Explicit bounds are validated before new
preparation. These optional additions preserve earlier plans and immutable history;
older closed-schema writers do not support authoring the additional fields.

Legacy prose using `line N` or `lines N-M` receives range diagnostics. Other locator
forms remain explicitly unresolved; they are not silently interpreted as verified.
Binary references require actual host inspection. Each source excerpt is bounded;
overlarge ranges return a request to narrow them rather than truncated evidence.
Report reads and preparation honor the same confined consumer paths.

Supplying an asset ID also compares the packet's selected requirements identity and
includes current production. The focused production `continuation` contains the exact
state hash, current task, provider/remote job identities with original discovery,
immediate action, prerequisites before another request, and outcome-dependent next
steps. Pending jobs require their original connection's observation/reconciliation.
Succeeded results lead to retrieval/import or candidate review before a correction
is proposed; actual unavailability can be recorded. A done task leads to delivery
review. Missing or stale selection remains explicit.

These are derived workflow instructions, not additional automatic approval rules.
The existing `new_request_allowed` field remains the local selection/pending advisory;
it does not mean the result was reviewed or another request is needed. Carry the
continuation into the caller result and reread after observations/state changes.
The report neither transfers a simulated job to a live service nor treats source-path
integration as renderer or artistic acceptance.

## Exact PLAR handoff snapshot

`pixl_plar_handoff` / `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --asset ID --requirements HASH
--expect STATE_HASH --root ROOT [--path plar.txt]` retains a consumer-owned JSON file
under `.pixl/handoffs/`, named by its byte hash. It verifies expected selected
requirements and production state, preserves the entire derived `resume` and its
immediate `next`, and stores agent-authored judgments under `details`. It returns the
snapshot path/hash and relevant identities. Identical input/state is idempotent;
changed details or state produce another snapshot. Corrupt existing bytes are rejected.

Details require an assignment `status` (delivered/partial/needs_input/blocked), with
other relevant artifacts/checks/reasoning fields chosen by the agent. Reserved derived
field names cannot be inserted at the top of details. Completed caller actions and
future work belong under their own details fields; they do not rewrite `resume` or
`next`. This is no automatic artistic verdict or completion certificate. State and
PLAR remain unchanged. The snapshot describes the observed point in time; reread the
selected asset before acting, especially after another agent changes it. A missing
production continuation leaves the ordinary allocation diagnostic usable without
manufacturing a stateful handoff. Existing handoff files remain supported as history.

1	# PIXL/2 normative specification
2	
3	PIXL/2 adds explicit intake and candidate acceptance to the existing agent-operated language. Its header is `PX2 <revision>`; value framing, bounds, identifiers, canonical ordering and record hashing follow [PIXL/1](PIXL-1.md). The enclosing canonical document includes its own format header. Existing PX1 files and the [PX1 registry](../pixl/registry.json) retain their original semantics.
4	
5	The complete PX2 field/type schema is [registry-v2.json](../pixl/registry-v2.json). Fields inherited unchanged from PX1 retain their defined meanings. Unknown kinds, fields and enum values fail. The JSON host adapter may include `format: 2`; absence means 1. The lifecycle commands never guess a format from fields. Library records can be copied with their complete dependency closure without changing record hashes; validate the destination document and its actual file paths.
6	
7	PX2 shares PX1's optional [library-source retention](library-retention.md): source resolution preserves the declared revision and reports its retained identity, while choice authority, adoption, candidate and verdict semantics remain unchanged.
8	
9	## Intake and concrete contracts
10	
11	P owns a list `in` of I choices and can retain the brief in `br`. Its `ct` is optional. Initialization via `intake` creates no C, dimensions, projection, palette or alpha defaults. The user is a valid A role. Old `init` remains a PX1 initializer for compatibility.
12	
13	I has an owning project `pr`, responsible actor `wh`, key `ky`, status `st`, value `vl`, source list `so` and rationale `wy`. Keys are unique within a project. Each I must appear in its P.in and cannot appear in another project's list. Status is one of:
14	
15	| Status | Required meaning |
16	|---|---|
17	| unresolved | `vl=?`; retain the missing choice or question in `wy` |
18	| observed | Non-null value with source evidence; an observation does not establish agreement |
19	| proposed | Non-null candidate value and rationale; sources can be absent |
20	| confirmed | Non-null value and supporting source, including a retained user instruction where applicable |
21	| conflict | At least two alternatives in `vl`, with sources/rationale preserving the disagreement |
22	
23	Confirmation is a recorded claim supported by sources, not authentication of the actor. A C is a concrete raster interpretation and can link its contributing choices through `ch`. When a linked choice is usable, a key naming an existing C field must have the same value as that field; custom aesthetic choices remain explicit semantic context. A previously concrete interpretation may remain recorded when its choice becomes unresolved/conflicting, but that contract cannot support active work until the conflict is resolved. This permits preserving old candidates and evidence while recording newly discovered uncertainty. Existing sources may intentionally use another contract.
24	
25	## Planned work and materialized candidates
26	
27	PX2 T has `ph` (research/sample/production/delivery), `ip` (existing X inputs), `op` (planned F outputs), `ca` (nominated X candidates) and `vr` (retained V verdicts), alongside `nm/ow/pr/dp/dc/kn/st`. PX1 task fields `io/ev` are not PX2 fields.
28	
29	F names a planned output and its kind, owning task `tk`, applicable requirements `rq`, and optional contract `ct`. T.op and F.tk must agree. F contains no invented file identity; it can exist before work produces a file. Each F requires at least one Q. A candidate X uses `of` to identify its F and must match its kind and contract. X always names actual bytes. Report/code/reference X may omit C; raster kinds cannot.
30	
31	Research and sample phases can investigate unproven K and can lack D. An open production/delivery task can plan before adoption; activation/completion requires an evidence-backed D and passing K scope coverage. D's research/proof requirements are unchanged. All active/done tasks require their prerequisites done. Raster output plans require a concrete C before activation, and unresolved/conflicting output choices block every phase. Sample work can test proposed/observed choices; production/delivery requires all choices in its output contracts confirmed. These choices must belong to the task's project. Input reference art can have another project's style and is not forced to adopt the output contract.
32	
33	`ready` returns only open tasks with satisfied local blockers. It never establishes remote availability or acceptance. `workflow` reports unresolved intake, per-task blockers and each planned output's candidates and requirement outcomes. A report can distinguish an unperformed check, a failed check and an unavailable check without changing state.
34	
35	## Required acceptance and retained verdicts
36	
37	Q declares an observable condition `ck`, owner `wh`, sources `so`, domain `dm` and required evidence mode `md`. Domains are mechanical, visual, continuity, engine and other. Visual criteria require visual mode; engine criteria require live mode. Other domains choose their applicable mode explicitly. There is no universal requirement that every output use every domain. Requirements belong to the plan and are stated before observing the candidate's results.
38	
39	V identifies a task, candidate X, required Q, reviewer, timestamp, rationale, status and supporting E receipts. Status is pass, fail or unavailable. Absence of a current V means unperformed. An unavailable verdict records the reason with no E and cannot accept anything. Only one non-superseded V may exist for a task/candidate/criterion combination; T.vr retains every V for that task.
40	
41	Current pass/fail verdicts require non-superseded E of the matching outcome and Q's required mode. Their combined bindings cover the candidate's full semantic scope and Q's full semantic scope. Thus evidence is bound to the actual X/F/C/I/Q/source revisions, not just an artifact name or a generic fixture. Receipt mode is a caller assertion backed by a retained file; live mode does not authenticate a service or engine. A provider response or bundled method POC cannot be substituted for a visual or engine acceptance obligation by reusing its old bindings.
42	
43	Semantic traversal in PX2 excludes P/E/T/J/N/V and includes I/F/Q as well as the original semantic kinds. Changing task states or superseding V therefore does not recursively change the evidence it summarizes. Changing a contract, applicable choice, plan or criterion invalidates live E bindings. Superseded V retains its old outcome and references but no longer requires current criterion membership or current E support. This permits an explicitly revised plan to retain historical rejected or obsolete requirements.
44	
45	A done task needs all prerequisite tasks done, at least one F, exactly one nominated X per F, and a current passing V for every Q on every nominee. Mechanical success alone cannot satisfy visual or engine criteria. Older rejected candidates remain recorded and do not prevent selecting a later candidate, but no unreviewed replacement inherits their proof.
46	
47	The optional [task completion operation](task-completion.md) nominates explicit already-reviewed candidates and publishes the existing active/done transitions. It retains all acceptance checks and creates no verdict or new UDL field.
48	
49	## Publication, amendment and resumption
50	
51	All PX1 concurrency, path confinement, immutable E and history publication guarantees remain. V fields are immutable after publication except one-way `ob=+`; correcting a verdict adds a new V ID. A newly introduced V cannot already be superseded: it must first pass current validation and be published, then a later revision may supersede it. Existing IDs cannot disappear. A store rejects format changes during commit. Existing PX1 stores are not automatically upgraded because old state does not identify confirmed choices or required acceptance. Start a new explicitly authored PX2 project when these operations are needed; preserve the old project as its own source/history.
52	
53	For each newly published pass/fail V, the planned F and its complete semantic scope, including Q and C/choices, must already exist unchanged in the immediately preceding saved state. Save planning/criterion changes before collecting and publishing results. Initial PX2 publication cannot contain pass/fail V. Unavailable observations do not claim evaluation and are exempt from this ordering rule. This establishes recorded ordering between a plan and its verdict; it cannot independently attest when a person actually inspected an image.
54	
55	A done task must reopen when it or its relevant dependency closure changes. PX2 closure does not traverse through P: an unrelated intake choice or project display name does not reopen an accepted sample. Link actual semantic dependencies through its input/output contracts, choices, criteria, sources and decisions. Changing one of those dependencies requires reopening and superseding stale E/V before new evaluation. History remains available for cold resumption.
56	
57	The optional [selected-asset preparation adapter](asset-preparation.md) authors the
58	existing candidate/sample records from exact reviewed PLAR artifacts and retains
59	input bytes. Its explicit versioned report-X metadata binding also checks current
60	PLAR identity before new job preparation/dispatch; it does not add record fields or
61	relabel an expert candidate interpretation as owner-approved production.
62	
63	## Operational boundaries
64	
65	The optional [candidate/family review adapter](candidate-review.md) retains explicit
66	observations through existing X/E/V, derives exact evidence scope and connects
67	nomination/completion with recoverable publication. It adds no registry fields;
68	prepared inspection packets retain their existing coverage contract.
69	
70	The optional [connected production-plan adapter](production-plan.md) authors
71	family/stage wiring from reviewed JSON and binds exact accepted upstream inputs
72	before preparing a staged request. It uses existing T/F/Q/X and PLAR metadata;
73	contracts, adoption, provider execution and acceptance keep their existing meaning.
74	
75	Use `intake`, `decode`, `encode`, `validate`, `commit`, `workflow`, `ready`, `context` and `impact` through the selected runner; MCP adds `pixl_intake` and `pixl_workflow`. `context` retains PX2 format and complete references. Mutable state and evidence live in the art project, outside installed resources. Generic encode/commit can author the declared records; they do not perform inspection or grant approval.
76	
77	This version supplies the local intake/sample lifecycle. The original platform prepare/job tools remain stateless local operations. Real PixelLab execution, actual visual judgments, destination-engine verification and model performance require their own observed evidence.
78	
79	## Durable provider jobs (registry 2.1.0 extension)
80	
81	J opts into durable history by supplying `jr` (current journal report X), `op` (nonempty distinct F outputs) and `xs` (all imported X candidates in event order, initially empty). J.xs preserves typed dependency closure for focused retrieval; these are not task nominations. Existing J without these fields retains its earlier semantics. A published legacy J cannot acquire this extension, and a durable J cannot shed it. Older PX2 readers reject these additional fields explicitly. PX1 schema and semantics are unchanged.
82	
83	The retained journal uses the version-1 closed JSON contract in [provider-recovery.md](provider-recovery.md). J.tk/tl/ah/si/ri/op must exactly project its task/tool/intent hash/state/remote identity/outputs. J.ev retains ordered local E receipts for every snapshot, starting with prepared intent and adding one snapshot per event. Each non-superseded local passing E binds exactly its immutable journal X and shares its path/hash. The last receipt binds J.jr. Such a pass establishes retention and local consistency; it is not remote, mechanical, visual or engine acceptance.
84	
85	Generic rooted validation replays the journal and every prefix, verifies local bytes and candidate bindings, and rejects invented projections. Publication requires a saved unchanged production plan before new prepared intent, one event per subsequent commit, immutable intent, immutable retained X/E, and unchanged imported candidates. No initial-state job can invent earlier submission history. Preparation and dispatch require satisfied task activation prerequisites and an open/active task. Another nonterminal durable attempt for an overlapping output, or an unjournaled nonterminal job for the task, blocks new preparation/dispatch.
86	
87	The local dispatch claim publishes `unknown` before returning the request to its host. It does not contact a service. Unknown work must be reconciled rather than resubmitted. Caller-supplied observations retain the returned identity and evidence; accepted states require an ID, which cannot change once recorded. Failed and succeeded are terminal except that success may import new candidates. Completion never follows from provider success: imported candidates still require their declared V criteria.
88	
89	Changed request context blocks dispatch but does not erase submitted history or prevent recording observations. Recovery reports list drift and next actions. Imports bind copied local bytes and the original output plan; a changed output plan must be reconciled before import. All operations use expected-hash publication. Unreferenced immutable blobs may remain after a failed commit; state.px is the sole publication authority. Local coordination cannot guarantee exactly-once remote execution or prevent a host from bypassing the procedure.
90	
91	## Family production and delivery (registry 2.2.0 extension)
92	
93	An optional F.bs names the exact X baseline for production or delivery. It is a semantic dependency, unlike the workflow-only T.ip. The baseline must belong to another sample task in the same project; its X is also listed in the consuming task's ip, and its task is a direct dp prerequisite. Open plans may preserve an unaccepted or replaced baseline. Activation/completion requires that exact sample still nominated and its task done. A sample's passing evidence does not automatically accept a family member.
94	
95	F.mb and F.ds together opt a report-kind output of a delivery task into the family operation and require bs. mb is a nonempty distinct ordered list of planned F members; ds is a nonempty distinct list of same-project I destination choices. Members cannot be the family output itself or another family output. They are the baseline's sample output or same-project production outputs sharing that exact bs. All member tasks are direct delivery prerequisites. A family declares at least one continuity Q, with project-specific mode/conditions; engine Q is declared when applicable. All destination choices must be confirmed for delivery activation/completion. Missing/unavailable engine acceptance remains separately represented through Q/V.
96	
97	A family manifest X has xs: baseline X first, then one selected X per member in the saved order (the baseline may also be a delivered member). xs belongs only to family report candidates and is required on every candidate of a family output. These references bind collective acceptance to the actual baseline, selected member identities, their plans/contracts and the destination/criteria scope. Merely listing siblings in T.ip does not supply this semantic proof.
98	
99	The [family delivery manifest contract](family-delivery.md) governs immutable copied files, saved-plan publication, historical membership and current acceptance. Existing family F cannot shed bs/mb/ds, and existing X cannot acquire fabricated snapshot history. Once published, a manifest X and its baseline/member X records are immutable; revisions add new candidate IDs. Changes to underlying contracts/requirements still require the existing supersession/reopening procedure.
100	
101	`family` / `pixl_family` reports baseline eligibility, member and collective acceptance, destination choices, pending provider attempts, saved snapshots and drift. `family-snapshot` / `pixl_family_snapshot` retains selected member bytes and publishes an unaccepted report candidate. It requires an open/active family task, the accepted baseline and all selected members on done tasks, no pending attempts for involved tasks, and the unchanged previously saved family plan. Snapshotting local files is allowed while destination/adoption/collective acceptance remains unresolved; it does not activate, nominate, evaluate or complete the delivery task. Actual artistic continuity and target-engine readiness require their own inspection and evidence.
102	
103	PLAR-bound continuation uses the [allocation/revision contract](asset-preparation.md#allocation-and-revised-work). Pending attempts for the same explicitly tagged asset exclude new jobs even under different task/output IDs. New task activation/completion checks the current selection and selected generation; retained historical validation is unchanged.

1	# Request and criteria handoff
2	
3	Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.
4	
5	## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract
6	
7	Use the focused authoring context described in [family delivery](family-delivery.md)
8	to locate current records before exploring histories. Keep a proposal's shared
9	source index once and reference its entries from individual clauses; preserve each
10	clause's authority, scope and exact locator. Do not duplicate whole reports in
11	every criterion, abbreviate literal checks into a group summary, or treat the
12	index's source class as requirement authority. Read the original source text for
13	the comparison; retrieve a complete record/history only where it bears on the
14	decision. Exact connected review remains the handoff for adoption.
15	
16	For a connected family/stage plan, use the adapter's returned `request_review`
17	arguments and retain that exact report as described in
18	[the connected handoff](#connected-family-and-stage-handoff). It supplies the saved
19	criteria and request evidence without manually rebuilding a candidate packet.
20	
21	For other contracts, save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:
22	
23	- `version`: 1.
24	- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Numbered locators refer to that individual file, never a concatenated multi-file terminal display. The caller verifies the cited content at those locators. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
25	- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
26	- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
27	- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
28	- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.
29	
30	Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.
31	
32	Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.
33	
34	Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.
35	
36	### Measured facts in creative requests
37	
38	Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.
39	
40	Keep centering calculations in one coordinate convention. For a half-open box
41	`[left, top, right, bottom]`, its centre in pixel-edge coordinates is
42	`((left + right) / 2, (top + bottom) / 2)` and the canvas centre is `(width / 2, height / 2)`.
43	A centroid computed from zero-based pixel indices needs `+0.5` per axis to use those
44	same edge coordinates. A margin imbalance, box-centre offset and mass-centroid offset
45	are different quantities; retain the actual calculation before calling an asset centred.
46	
47	The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.
48	
49	## Resolve source evidence for the comparison
50	
51	For candidate plans used by selected-asset preparation, call `pixl_request_review`
52	with the packet path and selected `asset_id` (CLI `request-review PACKET --asset ID
53	--root PROJECT`). It reads the exact request/criteria identities, returns cited text
54	with file-local bounds, and includes the current production continuation. It reports
55	invalid/unresolved locators and changed sources. A resolved excerpt is evidence for
56	the caller to interpret, not a consistency verdict. Retain this report with the review.
57	
58	Copy a host-spilled tool report as exact bytes before inspecting or formatting it.
59	These tool reports are UTF-8 JSON: use an explicit UTF-8 decoder (for example,
60	`Path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`), not the Windows process default. If saving a
61	formatted copy, compare its parsed value with the raw report before returning its
62	path/hash. A new file hash alone cannot detect text changed by a wrong decoder.
63	Keep the raw report alongside any formatted copy.
64	
65	When the connection is already discovered, bind `request.provider` and
66	`request.connection: {path, sha256}` to its exact artifact. Preparation compares that
67	reviewed connection with the supplied one; host credentials stay outside the artifact.
68	
69	Use `lines: [first,last]` on a criterion's source pointer when citing text; retain
70	`locator` as a human-readable label. Preparation validates explicit bounds before
71	saving new work. Numbered prose in older plans remains readable and receives
72	locator diagnostics. For non-text references inspect the actual image/animation;
73	for named sections resolve the location through the existing source tool. Do not
74	mark a locator verified merely because its claimed wording appears elsewhere.
75	
76	The optional criterion `authority` uses PLAR's requirement/proposal/observation/unknown
77	labels. Keep its basis and scope explicit. This label is an assertion to compare,
78	not an automatic grant of owner authority.

81	
82	### Connected family and stage handoff
83

85	for this same review tool. Pass that object to `pixl_request_review`; `packet`
86	names the store's `state.px`, `plan` names its exact connected-plan X, and `job`
87	is present after preparation. Existing plans can use those IDs directly. The

89	ID, record hash, literal check and source evidence. Authority starts unclassified:

91	identities remain visible so historical interpretation can be reviewed without
92	making an obsolete request current.
93

96	`criterion_comparisons` entry for **each** returned ID, including collective rules:

104	    "source_obligation": "What the cited source actually requires, with locator",
105	    "authority_basis": "Required outcome, scoped expert choice, observation, or mixed clauses",
106	    "scope": "The asset, stage or chosen construction this rule applies to",
107	    "literal_delta": "What the exact rule adds, drops or leaves unchanged",
108	    "discriminating_alternative": "A concrete alternative that tests that difference",
109	    "disposition": "Keep, clarify or correct, with the proposed artifact identity"
110	  }]
111	}
112	```
113	
114	Split mixed-authority clauses in these explanations. A sound construction does
115	not make every clause an owner requirement; nor does an expert choice need to be
116	removed merely because other valid methods exist. Keep the required artistic
117	outcome and identify the chosen method's narrower scope. Do not substitute one
118	grouped style/geometry assertion for this comparison.
119	
120	Call the same tool with `comparison` pointing to the saved caller file to check
121	coverage and identity. Missing, repeated, stale or incomplete rows are reported.
122	`complete:true` means structural coverage only; semantic judgment remains the
123	caller’s responsibility, and `consistent` stays null in the tool report. Record
124	the caller's own disposition separately. Save a corrected proposal beside the
125	old plan/request when necessary; do not rewrite historical criteria, transplant
126	acceptance or prepare another job merely to repair the review.
127	
128	### Compare the original sources and exact contract
129	
130	For either route, open the retained packet/report and verify its hashes. Read the original brief, relevant sources, complete request and complete criteria, not just the specialist's summary or self-audit. Check:
131	
132	1. Every explicit requirement survives into the request and relevant checks, including qualitative identity/style/state outcomes, actual reference role/input and consumer mapping. Check for dropped or weakened outcomes as well as added restrictions.
133	2. Every consequential extra restriction has its true basis and scope. Test whether a brief-conforming alternative would be rejected only because an observation or proposal was promoted to an owner requirement.
134	3. The proposed operation's actual declaration supports the payload. Do not infer a provider parameter, frame/direction count, alpha policy or camera from prose alone.
135	4. Findings concern these exact artifacts. Mechanical/hash validity and a specialist's consistency claim do not prove semantic agreement or artistic quality.
136	5. Each rejection rule belongs to the current candidate/stage and has satisfiable prerequisites. A first sample cannot require completed dependent family assets before it may be accepted. Retain deferred family or destination obligations with an explicit later stage in the handoff/PLAR; verify they remain scheduled rather than dropping the required outcome.
137	
138	For each rejection criterion, save one concise comparison using the following
139	sequence. A table or JSON is sufficient; this is the caller's actual reasoning about
140	the source, not a worksheet to have the specialist certify for itself.
141	
142	1. **Source obligation.** Derive the minimum required outcome from the original source
143	   wording and locator before using the draft criterion as its paraphrase. State what
144	   the source leaves open. For an expert criterion, identify the actual expert choice
145	   and candidate scope instead of inventing owner authority.
146	2. **Literal condition and additions.** Compare the entire check with that obligation.
147	   Identify the exact added or omitted words/clauses, including extent, composition,
148	   exclusions, comparisons and numerical bounds. A supported noun does not establish
149	   support for its modifiers. Read the check itself, not just its basis or label.
150	3. **Discriminating alternative.** For each added restriction, describe a plausible
151	   asset that keeps the source obligation true while making that specific restriction
152	   false. Name the clause being tested and whether the literal check would reject it.
153	   Merely changing a value the check already permits does not test that restriction.
154	   If the source itself excludes the alternative, identify the exact source support.
155	4. **Disposition.** Keep the required outcome; remove an unsupported narrowing from
156	   that rule or split it into an explicitly scoped expert choice with its own rationale.
157	   An ambiguous condition that could reject a valid alternative needs clearer wording;
158	   do not approve it by silently giving it a more permissive interpretation. Verify the
159	   correction in the returned artifact before marking the contract consistent.
160	
161	For example, a requirement for a readable silhouette does not itself require an
162	outlined silhouette. Comparing two outline colours leaves the added outline rule
163	untested; a readable outline-free construction tests it. The specialist may still
164	recommend an outline for this sample and explain its artistic value. The comparison
165	preserves that expertise while accurately describing who chose it and what it binds.
166	
167	Cover every rejection rule; group only genuinely identical ones. Retain the source
168	quote/bounds, literal delta, tested alternative and disposition together. A general
169	"the brief permits flexibility" statement or a prompt-choice label elsewhere cannot
170	cancel a restriction still present in an owner-authority acceptance condition.
171	
172	Check the **review route** as well as the wording. A local mechanical check can
173	establish measured dimensions, frame counts or alpha values. It cannot decide which
174	shape is intentional foreground, whether a matte is unwanted, whether a silhouette
175	reads as the requested symbol, or whether an accent serves its role. For a mixed
176	criterion, either split the measurement and required visual judgment or set its mode
177	to `visual` (normally domain `visual` too). The runtime requires saved native/enlarged
178	candidate views for visual-mode or visual/continuity-domain reviews; labelling such a
179	condition `mechanical`/`local` bypasses that evidence requirement. A planning-only
180	correction must still specify the route its future acceptance will actually need.
181	Do not call a corrected contract operable merely because its source locators resolve.
182	
183	When reviewing a specialist's response to a discrepancy, re-open the literal check.
184	An added attribution or a claim that a conventional construction excludes no valid
185	alternatives does not remove an unchanged mandatory recipe. Retain the source's
186	qualitative outcome as required and place the expert construction in a scoped proposal;
187	judge actual recognizability without declaring one geometric recipe universal.
188	
189	Resolve every evidence-report diagnostic before calling a locator verified. For a
190	text citation, open the actual source, use its file-local inclusive bounds and save
191	those bounds in the corrected packet; a nearby matching sentence does not repair a
192	wrong range. An unresolved named or visual reference needs actual inspection and a
193	recorded finding. A source hash alone never verifies the cited location or its meaning.
194	
195	The [delegation boundary](delegation.md#caller--specialist) distinguishes unchanged
196	historical evidence from the editable corrected proposal. A caller must not freeze
197	prior criterion text or authority in the new proposal; reassess those interpretations
198	against the source. Use the profile's visual-role distinctions when translating colour,
199	subject construction and transparency intent, rather than adding a construction rule.
200	
201	If a contract defect is found after delivery, preserve the original request, plan,
202	verdicts and candidate. Save a corrected proposal and independent comparison as a new
203	artifact, explicitly distinguishing it from the historical contract used for delivery.
204	Do not create another provider job merely to correct documentation, transplant old
205	verdicts to new criteria, or silently rewrite durable completed work. Carry both the
206	historical identity and the correction's adoption scope in the exact handoff details.
207	
208	Keep process requirements, output requirements and diagnostic proxies distinct. A required production route is checked through actual calls and downloaded-byte provenance; a property of the resulting image is evidence only when it establishes that claim. Do not silently turn a process restriction into an extra output-difference test, or a diagnostic into a rejection rule. Independent review uses the original source, not another agent's assertion that the rule is sourced.
209	
210	Save a concise `caller-review.json` (or equivalent named fields) with reviewer role, reviewed packet hash, `consistent` / `changes_requested` / `needs_input`, per-criterion comparisons and other findings tied to request locations and source evidence, and the next action. `consistent` means the planned contract matches this assignment; it is not provider execution or asset acceptance.
211	
212	If changes are needed, send the specialist the precise discrepancy and relevant source; preserve the original artifacts, revise only the affected contract, and inspect the returned new packet. Reuse the existing specialist when the host supports it. Resolve supplied facts yourself; ask the user only a consequential decision genuinely missing from the available context. No token, secret header or credential belongs in either file.
213	
214	If no independent caller/reviewer exists, retain the specialist's own review as self-review, proceed within existing authorization, and report the independent comparison as unperformed. Do not invent another agent or stop ordinary direct work solely to satisfy this procedure.
215	
216	## Carry the comparison through production
217	
218	Return `request_review` in the normal result, containing the packet and caller-review paths/hashes and unresolved findings. After preparing the durable provider job, verify its actual request still matches the reviewed arguments. A changed requirement, criterion or request needs a new comparison; polling progress and unrelated queue changes do not.
219	
220	The final caller opens the delivered assets, checks the actual request and output against this contract, and records its own observations. Keep contract consistency, provider outcome, visual quality and destination acceptance separate. For a rejected candidate, retain the failure and the revised request/criteria; changing a checker merely to pass the candidate is a contract change, not an asset correction.
221	
222	When an artistic explanation asserts a measurement, compare that assertion with
223	its actual data and coordinate convention. Reproducing a bounding box does not
224	verify a stated axis angle or arm-length ratio; approximate visual descriptions
225	should remain approximate. Correct an inconsistent explanation in a new observation
226	without converting its sample geometry into an additional rejection condition.
227	Reassess the original claim using its stated inputs. For quoted endpoints, retain
228	the coordinate convention and calculate their deltas, lengths and angles before
229	confirming an axis or ratio. Counts of occupied pixels, a bounding box and a newly
230	estimated centreline measure different things; they cannot confirm the original
231	endpoint claim. Save the old claim, calculation and corrected interpretation together
232	so the caller can reproduce the comparison without inheriting the earlier assertion.
233	
234	## Start a successor comparison with the concise view
235	
236	For two retained connected plans, call `pixl_request_review` with `view:"changes"`,
237	`plan` and explicit `against_plan`; CLI: `request-review STATE --plan NEW --against-plan OLD --view changes --root ROOT`.
238	Save with `result_path` / `--result-path`. Use the change counts, retained choices,
239	source drift and review attention to choose what to inspect. Then follow both
240	full-report retrievals and compare the exact literal criteria. The compact view
241	does not declare semantic equivalence, direct succession, consistency or approval.
242	All old/new IDs/hashes remain indexed; renamed clauses require explicit mapping.
243	
244	Focused `pixl_context(view:"authoring")` expands explicitly linked choices and
245	their authority dependencies. Inspect `choice_scope.other_intake` when an unlinked
246	caller choice may apply; its retrieval links preserve access to the full record.
247	Do not promote observed/proposed values to confirmed requirements or infer that
248	an omitted full value is irrelevant. Keep the independent caller's interpretation
249	separate from the tool's deterministic structural comparison.

81	selected asset before acting, especially after another agent changes it. A missing
82	production continuation leaves the ordinary allocation diagnostic usable without
83	manufacturing a stateful handoff. Existing handoff files remain supported as history.

1	# Provider recovery journal version 1
2	
3	This is the normative external-file contract for the opt-in [PX2 durable J](PIXL-2.md) extension. Files are UTF-8 canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, no ASCII escaping, finite values) followed by one LF. Hashes are SHA-256 of exact bytes unless described as a canonical JSON value hash (which omits the final LF). Every object has closed fields; arbitrary supplied evidence and argument values remain bounded JSON objects.
4	
5	The top-level fields are `version` (integer 1), `intent`, `intent_sha256` (canonical value hash of intent), `events`, `state`, `remote_id`. Intent has `job` (PIXL identifier), `request`, `context`. Context has `task`, distinct nonempty `outputs`, `task_sha256` and `bindings` (record IDs to hashes, including every output). Task hash covers its record without mutable st/ca/vr. Bindings cover selected outputs and the semantic closure of task inputs, decisions and methods. Context is immutable after preparation.
6	
7	Request fields are `version` (1), `provider`, `tool`, `arguments`, `schema`, `schema_sha256`, `request_sha256`, `discovery`, `authorization`, `prepared_at`, `policy` (`caller_schema`), `remote_executed` (false), `cached_assessment`. Request hash covers the provider/tool/arguments/schema object. The exact supplied schema governs argument validation. Discovery has source, observed_at and nonempty evidence. Authorization has scope and nonempty evidence. Dates are ISO timestamps. Provider/tool/source/scope are nonempty strings. These are caller assertions; they neither authenticate a remote service nor grant additional authority.
8	
9	New request preparation rejects a discovery observation later than the local preparation clock. This check applies before publishing new intent; existing version-1 histories retain their original caller assertions and remain readable without rewriting their bytes.
10	
11	Cached assessment is a retained advisory result, never recomputed to reinterpret old intent. It has advisory=true, source, retrieved_at, status and findings. Status describes passed/conflict/unlisted/unavailable/not_applicable; findings contain code/detail. A caller-schema-valid request may report a cache conflict without rewriting arguments or claiming the cache is current. Credential fields in supplied values are rejected. This is a field-name guard, not detection of every secret that could be embedded in prose.
12	
13	Each event has `sequence` (1-based contiguous integer), `event`, `recorded_at`, `remote_id`, nonempty `evidence`, and `artifact`. Artifact is null except for imported, where it has `id`, `output`, `record_sha256`. The candidate ID is unique in the journal, and output must belong to intent. State and identity are derived by replay; they cannot be edited independently. All request and event timestamps require an explicit UTC offset and support at most six fractional-second digits. Event instants cannot run backward or precede preparation; different offset spellings of the same instant are permitted. Unsupported precision is rejected without truncation. Evidence remains caller-supplied data.
14	
15	Dispatch occurs once from prepared, has no remote ID and yields unknown. Before dispatch, only failed may abandon preparation. After dispatch, submitted/running/unknown observations may repeat; running cannot regress to submitted, including through unknown. Accepted states submitted/running/succeeded require an observed ID. Once known, that ID remains identical on every later event. Succeeded and failed are terminal for observations. Imported is allowed only after succeeded and retains that state and identity. No event permits returning to prepared. A retry is a new authorized intent, after prior pending work has been reconciled.
16	
17	The complete prefix history is retained through successive J.ev receipts and immutable journal X files. Each update publishes one additional event and one new snapshot; no prefix can be rewritten or omitted. An imported artifact's current X record hash must match its retained event.
