# Provider recovery journal version 1

This is the normative external-file contract for the opt-in [PX2 durable J](PIXL-2.md) extension. Files are UTF-8 canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, no ASCII escaping, finite values) followed by one LF. Hashes are SHA-256 of exact bytes unless described as a canonical JSON value hash (which omits the final LF). Every object has closed fields; arbitrary supplied evidence and argument values remain bounded JSON objects.

The top-level fields are `version` (integer 1), `intent`, `intent_sha256` (canonical value hash of intent), `events`, `state`, `remote_id`. Intent has `job` (PIXL identifier), `request`, `context`. Context has `task`, distinct nonempty `outputs`, `task_sha256` and `bindings` (record IDs to hashes, including every output). Task hash covers its record without mutable st/ca/vr. Bindings cover selected outputs and the semantic closure of task inputs, decisions and methods. Context is immutable after preparation.

Request fields are `version` (1), `provider`, `tool`, `arguments`, `schema`, `schema_sha256`, `request_sha256`, `discovery`, `authorization`, `prepared_at`, `policy` (`caller_schema`), `remote_executed` (false), `cached_assessment`. Request hash covers the provider/tool/arguments/schema object. The exact supplied schema governs argument validation. Discovery has source, observed_at and nonempty evidence. Authorization has scope and nonempty evidence. Dates are ISO timestamps. Provider/tool/source/scope are nonempty strings. These are caller assertions; they neither authenticate a remote service nor grant additional authority.

New request preparation rejects a discovery observation later than the local preparation clock. This check applies before publishing new intent; existing version-1 histories retain their original caller assertions and remain readable without rewriting their bytes.

Cached assessment is a retained advisory result, never recomputed to reinterpret old intent. It has advisory=true, source, retrieved_at, status and findings. Status describes passed/conflict/unlisted/unavailable/not_applicable; findings contain code/detail. A caller-schema-valid request may report a cache conflict without rewriting arguments or claiming the cache is current. Credential fields in supplied values are rejected. This is a field-name guard, not detection of every secret that could be embedded in prose.

Each event has `sequence` (1-based contiguous integer), `event`, `recorded_at`, `remote_id`, nonempty `evidence`, and `artifact`. Artifact is null except for imported, where it has `id`, `output`, `record_sha256`. The candidate ID is unique in the journal, and output must belong to intent. State and identity are derived by replay; they cannot be edited independently. All request and event timestamps require an explicit UTC offset and support at most six fractional-second digits. Event instants cannot run backward or precede preparation; different offset spellings of the same instant are permitted. Unsupported precision is rejected without truncation. Evidence remains caller-supplied data.

Dispatch occurs once from prepared, has no remote ID and yields unknown. Before dispatch, only failed may abandon preparation. After dispatch, submitted/running/unknown observations may repeat; running cannot regress to submitted, including through unknown. Accepted states submitted/running/succeeded require an observed ID. Once known, that ID remains identical on every later event. Succeeded and failed are terminal for observations. Imported is allowed only after succeeded and retains that state and identity. No event permits returning to prepared. A retry is a new authorized intent, after prior pending work has been reconciled.

The complete prefix history is retained through successive J.ev receipts and immutable journal X files. Each update publishes one additional event and one new snapshot; no prefix can be rewritten or omitted. An imported artifact's current X record hash must match its retained event. Publication checks the unchanged F plan before linking a new candidate. These guarantees establish local history and relationships, not the actual truth of remote observations or artistic acceptance.

Plans created by [selected-asset preparation](asset-preparation.md) opt into an explicit
`pixl.plar.selection/1` report-X input binding. Its current PLAR requirements identity
is checked at new intent/dispatch publication, including generic commits. Retained
input bytes keep reports and reconciliation of existing submissions available after
consumer changes. Job reports expose selection state without rewriting the immutable
intent. This adds no journal field and does not reinterpret legacy untagged inputs.

PLAR-bound continuation uses the [allocation/revision contract](asset-preparation.md#allocation-and-revised-work). Pending attempts for the same explicitly tagged asset exclude new jobs even under different task/output IDs. New task activation/completion checks the current selection and selected generation; retained historical validation is unchanged.

## Recovery reports and local retries

The existing `jobs` report adds a read-only `recovery` projection to each durable
job: `action`, originating `provider`/`tool`, immutable observed `remote_id`,
`missing_outputs`, `imported` and `guidance`. Each imported entry identifies
`candidate_id`, `output_id`, retained project-relative `path`, file `sha256` and
`record_sha256`. It projects the validated journal and actual artifact records;
it does not authenticate the provider, grant dispatch or accept candidates.
Legacy unjournaled jobs retain their manual-history route.

Succeeded jobs with any planned output not yet imported report
`next_action: retrieve_outputs`; a partial set of imports is not complete
retrieval. Once every requested output has at least one imported candidate, the
next action is `inspect_candidates`, using current acceptance separately. Unknown
jobs still require reconciliation through their originating connection, with or
without an observed ID. Submitted/running jobs require observation of that exact
identity; neither missing IDs nor elapsed time permit another dispatch.

An import reply can be lost after publication. After rereading the current state
hash, the same `job-import` may return `reused_import: true` with unchanged
hash/revision and no new event or blob. This requires the same job's already
retained imported event, output and candidate record identity, unchanged current
output context, equal source-file bytes and canonically identical import evidence.
The source file's original textual path is not in the journal; an equivalent
local file is allowed, without claiming directed ancestry from its path. An
existing candidate from another job, changed bytes/evidence/output/context, or
stale expected hash still fails. Fresh imports return `reused_import: false`.

The optional HTTP adapter materializes its fully retained, validated succeeded
PNG response atomically before candidate publication. A conflicting or partial
old download is preserved in place; verified response bytes are retained under a
separate deterministic recovery path. The returned `download` gives the actual
path/hash/size, whether that download was reused, and the preserved old
`recovered_from` path/hash/size when applicable. Conflicting recovery-path bytes
are refused rather than overwritten. This local repair uses no new provider call,
changes no journal field, and grants no artifact acceptance. Interruption between
download retention and candidate publication may leave an unreferenced complete
file, which a cold retry can reuse under the normal expected-hash rules.

1	# Candidate and family review authoring, version 1
2	
3	This adapter publishes explicit specialist judgments through existing PX2 X/E/V
4	records and task completion. It adds no UDL fields or automatic artistic judgment.
5	It supports saved raster candidates and saved family manifest candidates equally.
6	The existing inspection-packet operation and its view-coverage rules are unchanged.
7	Use that operation for prepared-packet viewing; use this operation for actual
8	project observations such as recorded playback, collective views and renderer reports.
9	
10	## Read the exact review target
11	
12	`review-context STATE CANDIDATE --root ROOT` / `pixl_review_context` returns current
13	canonical `state_hash`, semantic `binding_hash`, candidate file SHA-256, owning
14	task/output, literal criteria and their current verdict IDs, nomination and task
15	status. Family context also identifies the immutable manifest and retained members;
16	its `snapshot_acceptance` describes creation, while `current_acceptance` describes
17	the current criteria and task. Neither is an inferred aesthetic judgment.
18	
19	## Publish one explicit review
20	
21	`candidate-review STORE CANDIDATE REVIEW_ID REVIEW_JSON --expect STATE_HASH --root ROOT`
22	and `pixl_candidate_review` use the same closed JSON observation:
23	
24	```json
25	{
26	  "version": 1,
27	  "binding_hash": "FROM_REVIEW_CONTEXT",
28	  "reviewer": "EXISTING_ACTOR_ID",
29	  "observed_at": "2026-11-09T16:00:00+00:00",
30	  "observations": [
31	    {"path":"work/playback.png","sha256":"ACTUAL_FILE_HASH","mode":"visual","note":"What the reviewer actually saw, including scale and sequence scope."},
32	    {"path":"work/render.json","sha256":"ACTUAL_FILE_HASH","mode":"live","note":"What the actual destination execution established."}
33	  ],
34	  "verdicts": [
35	    {"criterion":"CURRENT_Q_ID","status":"pass","reason":"Judgment against the literal check.","supersedes":null,"observations":[0]}
36	  ],
37	  "action": "record",
38	  "next_action": "Review the remaining destination criterion.",
39	  "limitations": []
40	}
41	```
42	
43	`observed_at` is a caller-declared timezone-aware observation time no later than
44	recording; it is not generated viewing history. Each performed verdict references
45	one or more distinct observations of its required evidence mode (`local`, `visual`
46	or `live`). Unavailable verdicts have no observation indices and create no E.
47	Each supplied criterion must belong to this output. `supersedes` names its exact
48	current V or is null when none exists. Omitted criteria retain their current state.
49	Reasons, observations, next action and limitations remain specialist-authored.
50	An evidence file or schema alone cannot establish that the observation occurred.
51	
52	`action` is explicit: `record` retains judgments; `nominate` also selects this
53	candidate for its output, preserving other output selections; `complete` also
54	performs the existing task-completion checks/transitions. Completion needs every
55	output nominated and every required criterion passing, current allocation,
56	activation prerequisites and resolved pending jobs. A failed/unavailable review
57	is retained with record/nominate; asking to complete it fails before publication.
58	Already-done work must be explicitly reopened before a new review.
59	
60	The current canonical state hash protects publication. The semantic binding hash
61	protects the candidate, output/criteria and their complete semantic dependencies
62	even if a caller refreshes the state hash after a contract change. File SHA-256
63	values protect the observations. The adapter derives E scope, IDs and record
64	bindings; callers do not construct records or calculate a canonical state digest.
65	
66	## Retention, retries and limits
67	
68	Files are captured and copied under `STORE/reviews/<report-sha256>/`; the canonical
69	report contains the request, original paths, retained identities and source state.
70	Auxiliary X records bind retained files, and E binds the report plus candidate/Q
71	semantic scope. Report/file IDs are derived from REVIEW_ID. No supplied source
72	or previous evidence is overwritten. Maximum 64 observations, 64 MiB per file,
73	256 MiB aggregate and 1,024 declared verdicts; reports retain the codec size limit.
74	
75	The operation holds the store lock, checks the complete review/nomination/completion
76	sequence before publishing, then saves ordinary revisions. An interruption may
77	leave immutable unreferenced files or a retained review before completion. Reload
78	the current state hash and repeat the **same REVIEW_ID and observation** to finish;
79	existing review/verdict IDs are reused. Changed payloads, stale bindings or
80	superseded reviews cannot be replayed as new acceptance. A retry never submits a
81	provider job. Changing the review requires a new ID and explicit supersession.
82	
83	Results expose `state_hash` (canonical state), `review_sha256` (report file), current
84	criteria/nomination/task status and publication steps. Immutable snapshot creation
85	status stays separate from current acceptance. The report does not attest reviewer
86	identity, actual viewing or renderer honesty; retained host/runner evidence supplies
87	those observations. Generic source amendment and historical supersession retain
88	their existing PX2 semantics.
89	
90	## Save results directly
91	
92	Use CLI `--result-path work/review-result.json` or MCP `result_path` to save the
93	complete result without transcribing JSON, Windows paths or hashes. The option is
94	available for context, request-review, review-context, candidate-review, family,
95	family-snapshot and PLAR handoff. The path is relative to the explicit consumer
96	root and must be fresh; an existing destination is rejected before the operation.
97	The response contains `result_saved`, the path, file SHA-256, byte count and key
98	status fields. Read the saved file for complete criteria and publication details.
99	CLI full wire context remains PX text; other listed exports contain JSON.
100	
101	If writing fails after an operation publishes, the response has
102	`result_saved:false` and includes the actual `operation_result` (and `wire_result`
103	for wire context). CLI returns a nonzero exit code. Reconcile that result with
104	current state before retrying; a failed file export does not undo publication.
105	Use a fresh path and the operation's existing retry rules. Default output without
106	this option is unchanged; exports do not alter the saved-state format.
107

1	# Agent-to-agent asset work
2	
3	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
4	
5	## Caller → specialist
6	
7	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
8	
9	| Context | What the specialist needs |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
12	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
13	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
14	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
15	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
16	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
17	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
18	
19	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.
20	
21	For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.
22	
23	The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.
24	
25	When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
26	the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
27	criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
28	**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
29	scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
30	Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
31	A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
32	requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
33	also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
34	explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
35	Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.
36	
37	For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
38	when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
39	uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
40	Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
41	from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
42	assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
43	and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
44	claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.
45	
46	When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
47	critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
48	Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
49	message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
50	Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
51	caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
52	that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
53	child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
54	an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
55	foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
56	depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
57	changing the user's global configuration.
58	
59	A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.
60	
61	## Specialist → caller while working
62	
63	Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.
64	
65	Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.
66	
67	Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.
68	
69	Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.
70	
71	## Specialist → caller at completion
72	
73	Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
74	PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
75	of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
76	from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
77	without manufacturing PLAR or production records:
78	
79	- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
80	- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
81	- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
82	- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
83	- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
84	- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
85	- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.
86	
87	When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.
88	
89	Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.
90	
91	Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.
92

# Agent-to-agent asset work

Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.

## Caller → specialist

Supply the smallest complete assignment:

| Context | What the specialist needs |
| --- | --- |
| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |

Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.

For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.

The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.

When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.

For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.

When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
changing the user's global configuration.

A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.

## Specialist → caller while working

Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.

Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.

Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.

Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.

## Specialist → caller at completion

Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
without manufacturing PLAR or production records:

- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.

When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.

Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.

Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.

The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.

For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`,
`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The
selected read's top-level `hash` identifies the PLAR file, not production state.
CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --path QUEUE --asset ID
--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --view caller --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
Return the caller view and its exact handoff locator; the caller opens the retained
file and compares its state identity with fresh focused PLAR. Omitting `--view caller`
keeps the existing receipt response. The view does not add acceptance or alter the
saved handoff. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
Before returning a reviewed open task, check its current nominee and workflow
requirements. Saved verdicts on an unselected candidate do not describe the
active output. Nominate the intended candidate through normal state authoring
when appropriate; preserve unavailable verdicts and leave the task open.

`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.

Use optional `details.caller` for the bounded ordinary return: summary, artifact
and report locators, issues and integration findings, following its closed
[contract](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md). Retain complete observations
in the other details fields and referenced files. Each declared file reference
contains exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`; the runtime verifies its current
confined file bytes before publishing. These checks do not verify the role or
judgment you supplied. The caller view distinguishes
these authored claims from derived task, acceptance and continuation facts.
A missing integration observation stays unreported; an accepted candidate does
not manufacture an assignment-status or integration claim. Without `details.caller`,
`caller.present` is false and the full details remain retrievable; legacy prose is
not automatically summarized.

For example, only when the assigned destination inspection remains unperformed:

```json
{
  "status": "partial",
  "caller": {
    "summary": "Candidate bytes are retained; required destination inspection remains unperformed.",
    "integration": {
      "status": "not_performed",
      "summary": "No destination observation has been made for this assignment."
    },
    "issues": [
      {
        "category": "unfinished_work",
        "summary": "The assigned destination check has not run.",
        "recovery": "Run the assigned destination check, retain its actual evidence and refresh the handoff."
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Use actual findings and omit inapplicable fields. Summary/recovery text is bounded
to 600 characters; artifact, report, issue and integration-evidence arrays each
hold at most 12 entries, and the complete caller block at most 8192 compact UTF-8
JSON bytes. Move detail to linked files instead of truncating obligations.
Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
`not_in_scope`; omission is not one of those observations.

Follow the returned full-handoff, details and resume locators for exact retrieval.
Read `resume_inline`: the unchanged `resume` is present up to 4096 compact UTF-8
JSON bytes; otherwise `resume_ref` retrieves it in full. It is never rewritten or
truncated. `details_ref` and `resume_ref` identify physical source ranges and JSON
pointers in the same immutable handoff. Use its `path`/`sha256` for the full file.
These facts describe the captured selection; use the returned `refresh` read
after source or state changes, and reconcile the current identities. Read that full resume before acting on its jobs or
recovery instructions. Keep routine responses useful without pasting the complete
criteria audit, request report or tool transcript into the return.

On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can

1	# Preserve artistic requirement authority
2	
3	Read when translating an aesthetic brief into prompts, rejection criteria, or a review. The cases below document observed failure modes; their measured values are not universal pixel-art rules.
4	
5	For delegated work, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md) so the caller can inspect the actual artifacts independently. A self-audit is useful correction work, but its conclusion is not the caller's acceptance.
6	
7	Every production approach carries a compact authority table: property/value, requirement versus observation/proposal, exact source, and applicable scope. Carry the user's requested aesthetic into the derived prompts and checks. An image interpretation that differs from the brief is a reported uncertainty, not permission to replace that treatment. Only established project requirements become production rejection rules; proposals define labeled experiments. A measured color, gap, alpha level, component count or diagnostic contrast result remains an observation until adopted. Before the final handoff, reconcile every enforced restriction in the whole approach with that table; remove unsupported approval claims and keep diagnostic conclusions within their tested conditions.
8	
9	When the brief specifies a treatment, the proposed sample, production instructions and review criteria must all explicitly retain it. For requested selective anti-aliasing and partial transparency, describe where those treatments will be authored and how they will be reviewed; a reference interpretation such as “glow” does not replace either requirement. Uncertainty about a new shape calls for a treatment-preserving experiment, not a default ban on that shape or treatment. When no fixed palette is imposed, production checks omit exact palette membership; a palette experiment remains optional. Describe matching quality, lighting intent and provider reliability as interpretations or untested expectations unless evidence establishes them. A plan or a copied reference recipe cannot guarantee those outcomes.
10	
11	Test each derived restriction against a variation that still satisfies the brief. If that variation could fail the check, the extra restriction is a proposal, not an entailed requirement. Two detached antenna islands, for example, do not forbid another intentional detached detail or require the reference's total component count, coordinates or gap rows. Apply the same scope check to planned failure conclusions: one failed candidate establishes that attempt's failure, not a provider's general inability. A fallback can address that attempt without claiming a universal limit.
12	
13	After saving an approach, reopen and read the complete file before the final response. Audit the actual provider prompt, every proposed rejection check and every fallback conclusion against the authority table; reviewing the table or selected sections alone does not complete this step. For each added restriction, either identify its adopted source or label it as an optional experiment and remove it from production rejection rules. In a proposed experimental prompt, label the extra choices as proposals at the prompt itself. Correct contradictions such as an open alpha policy followed by an unexplained “no antialiasing” directive, or a qualitative color requirement turned into an invented numeric hue threshold. Preserve the earlier draft when revising it and report the scope and any unresolved conflict from this whole-file audit.
14	
15

# Next production assignment: revise art in its actual destination

Use the animation and terrain adapters when the next real asset assignment fits
their explicit contracts. The existing CF-10 robot directional consumer remains
available for directional requirements. Select the useful domain from actual
project need; do not submit paid jobs merely to populate a coverage count.

1. Retain the caller's reference intent, current source declarations, authorized
   scope, actual provider job/output identity, original bytes and current family
   selection. Derive dimensions, timing, pivots and tile convention from that
   project. Do not inherit this diagnostic project's values as universal rules.
2. Bind all members to their actual served destinations. Execute the applicable
   fixed profile and retain its report, stills, observed playback or neighborhoods,
   source closure, exact files and cleanup. Keep mechanical success distinct from
   the visual requirements and any unresolved destination limits.
3. Inspect actual returned art at native scale and contextual enlargement. For
   animation, explain readable silhouette, intended motion and contact continuity
   across the declared timing and anchor. For terrain, explain material joins and
   corner intent in the agreed neighborhoods. For directions, inspect orientation
   and cross-direction identity in the robot consumer or a justified successor.
4. Identify a useful defect and a scoped correction with a reason tied to the
   intended use. Preserve valid unrelated assets. Use the authorized production
   workflow to revise, retaining the original request, failure and exact successor.
5. Re-execute the affected destination and compare actual old/new pixels under
   the same contract. Record which visual criterion improved and any remaining
   weakness. Explicit specialist/caller review is separate from renderer checks;
   human acceptance stays separately unrecorded until actually supplied.

CF-09 closes only on a useful actual-art revision and its observed destination
outcome. Controlled fixtures, provider completion, test totals and screenshots
alone do not close it. M1/M2 and broader M3/M4 remain open.

1	# Provider recovery journal version 1
2	
3	This is the normative external-file contract for the opt-in [PX2 durable J](PIXL-2.md) extension. Files are UTF-8 canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, no ASCII escaping, finite values) followed by one LF. Hashes are SHA-256 of exact bytes unless described as a canonical JSON value hash (which omits the final LF). Every object has closed fields; arbitrary supplied evidence and argument values remain bounded JSON objects.
4	
5	The top-level fields are `version` (integer 1), `intent`, `intent_sha256` (canonical value hash of intent), `events`, `state`, `remote_id`. Intent has `job` (PIXL identifier), `request`, `context`. Context has `task`, distinct nonempty `outputs`, `task_sha256` and `bindings` (record IDs to hashes, including every output). Task hash covers its record without mutable st/ca/vr. Bindings cover selected outputs and the semantic closure of task inputs, decisions and methods. Context is immutable after preparation.
6	
7	Request fields are `version` (1), `provider`, `tool`, `arguments`, `schema`, `schema_sha256`, `request_sha256`, `discovery`, `authorization`, `prepared_at`, `policy` (`caller_schema`), `remote_executed` (false), `cached_assessment`. Request hash covers the provider/tool/arguments/schema object. The exact supplied schema governs argument validation. Discovery has source, observed_at and nonempty evidence. Authorization has scope and nonempty evidence. Dates are ISO timestamps. Provider/tool/source/scope are nonempty strings. These are caller assertions; they neither authenticate a remote service nor grant additional authority.
8	
9	New request preparation rejects a discovery observation later than the local preparation clock. This check applies before publishing new intent; existing version-1 histories retain their original caller assertions and remain readable without rewriting their bytes.
10	
11	Cached assessment is a retained advisory result, never recomputed to reinterpret old intent. It has advisory=true, source, retrieved_at, status and findings. Status describes passed/conflict/unlisted/unavailable/not_applicable; findings contain code/detail. A caller-schema-valid request may report a cache conflict without rewriting arguments or claiming the cache is current. Credential fields in supplied values are rejected. This is a field-name guard, not detection of every secret that could be embedded in prose.
12	
13	Each event has `sequence` (1-based contiguous integer), `event`, `recorded_at`, `remote_id`, nonempty `evidence`, and `artifact`. Artifact is null except for imported, where it has `id`, `output`, `record_sha256`. The candidate ID is unique in the journal, and output must belong to intent. State and identity are derived by replay; they cannot be edited independently. All request and event timestamps require an explicit UTC offset and support at most six fractional-second digits. Event instants cannot run backward or precede preparation; different offset spellings of the same instant are permitted. Unsupported precision is rejected without truncation. Evidence remains caller-supplied data.
14	
15	Dispatch occurs once from prepared, has no remote ID and yields unknown. Before dispatch, only failed may abandon preparation. After dispatch, submitted/running/unknown observations may repeat; running cannot regress to submitted, including through unknown. Accepted states submitted/running/succeeded require an observed ID. Once known, that ID remains identical on every later event. Succeeded and failed are terminal for observations. Imported is allowed only after succeeded and retains that state and identity. No event permits returning to prepared. A retry is a new authorized intent, after prior pending work has been reconciled.
16	
17	The complete prefix history is retained through successive J.ev receipts and immutable journal X files. Each update publishes one additional event and one new snapshot; no prefix can be rewritten or omitted. An imported artifact's current X record hash must match its retained event. Publication checks the unchanged F plan before linking a new candidate. These guarantees establish local history and relationships, not the actual truth of remote observations or artistic acceptance.
18	
19	Plans created by [selected-asset preparation](asset-preparation.md) opt into an explicit
20	`pixl.plar.selection/1` report-X input binding. Its current PLAR requirements identity
21	is checked at new intent/dispatch publication, including generic commits. Retained
22	input bytes keep reports and reconciliation of existing submissions available after
23	consumer changes. Job reports expose selection state without rewriting the immutable
24	intent. This adds no journal field and does not reinterpret legacy untagged inputs.
25	
26	PLAR-bound continuation uses the [allocation/revision contract](asset-preparation.md#allocation-and-revised-work). Pending attempts for the same explicitly tagged asset exclude new jobs even under different task/output IDs. New task activation/completion checks the current selection and selected generation; retained historical validation is unchanged.
27	
28	## Recovery reports and local retries
29	
30	The existing `jobs` report adds a read-only `recovery` projection to each durable
31	job: `action`, originating `provider`/`tool`, immutable observed `remote_id`,
32	`missing_outputs`, `imported` and `guidance`. Each imported entry identifies
33	`candidate_id`, `output_id`, retained project-relative `path`, file `sha256` and
34	`record_sha256`. It projects the validated journal and actual artifact records;
35	it does not authenticate the provider, grant dispatch or accept candidates.
36	Legacy unjournaled jobs retain their manual-history route.
37	
38	Succeeded jobs with any planned output not yet imported report
39	`next_action: retrieve_outputs`; a partial set of imports is not complete
40	retrieval. Once every requested output has at least one imported candidate, the
41	next action is `inspect_candidates`, using current acceptance separately. Unknown
42	jobs still require reconciliation through their originating connection, with or
43	without an observed ID. Submitted/running jobs require observation of that exact
44	identity; neither missing IDs nor elapsed time permit another dispatch.
45	
46	An import reply can be lost after publication. After rereading the current state
47	hash, the same `job-import` may return `reused_import: true` with unchanged
48	hash/revision and no new event or blob. This requires the same job's already
49	retained imported event, output and candidate record identity, unchanged current
50	output context, equal source-file bytes and canonically identical import evidence.
51	The source file's original textual path is not in the journal; an equivalent
52	local file is allowed, without claiming directed ancestry from its path. An
53	existing candidate from another job, changed bytes/evidence/output/context, or
54	stale expected hash still fails. Fresh imports return `reused_import: false`.
55	
56	The optional HTTP adapter materializes its fully retained, validated succeeded
57	PNG response atomically before candidate publication. A conflicting or partial
58	old download is preserved in place; verified response bytes are retained under a
59	separate deterministic recovery path. The returned `download` gives the actual
60	path/hash/size, whether that download was reused, and the preserved old
61	`recovered_from` path/hash/size when applicable. Conflicting recovery-path bytes
62	are refused rather than overwritten. This local repair uses no new provider call,
63	changes no journal field, and grants no artifact acceptance. Interruption between
64	download retention and candidate publication may leave an unreferenced complete
65	file, which a cold retry can reuse under the normal expected-hash rules.

1	# Candidate and family review authoring, version 1
2	
3	This adapter publishes explicit specialist judgments through existing PX2 X/E/V
4	records and task completion. It adds no UDL fields or automatic artistic judgment.
5	It supports saved raster candidates and saved family manifest candidates equally.
6	The existing inspection-packet operation and its view-coverage rules are unchanged.
7	Use that operation for prepared-packet viewing; use this operation for actual
8	project observations such as recorded playback, collective views and renderer reports.
9	
10	## Read the exact review target
11	
12	`review-context STATE CANDIDATE --root ROOT` / `pixl_review_context` returns current
13	canonical `state_hash`, semantic `binding_hash`, candidate file SHA-256, owning
14	task/output, literal criteria and their current verdict IDs, nomination and task
15	status. Family context also identifies the immutable manifest and retained members;
16	its `snapshot_acceptance` describes creation, while `current_acceptance` describes
17	the current criteria and task. Neither is an inferred aesthetic judgment.
18	
19	## Publish one explicit review
20	
21	`candidate-review STORE CANDIDATE REVIEW_ID REVIEW_JSON --expect STATE_HASH --root ROOT`
22	and `pixl_candidate_review` use the same closed JSON observation:
23	
24	```json
25	{
26	  "version": 1,
27	  "binding_hash": "FROM_REVIEW_CONTEXT",
28	  "reviewer": "EXISTING_ACTOR_ID",
29	  "observed_at": "2026-11-09T16:00:00+00:00",
30	  "observations": [
31	    {"path":"work/playback.png","sha256":"ACTUAL_FILE_HASH","mode":"visual","note":"What the reviewer actually saw, including scale and sequence scope."},
32	    {"path":"work/render.json","sha256":"ACTUAL_FILE_HASH","mode":"live","note":"What the actual destination execution established."}
33	  ],
34	  "verdicts": [
35	    {"criterion":"CURRENT_Q_ID","status":"pass","reason":"Judgment against the literal check.","supersedes":null,"observations":[0]}
36	  ],
37	  "action": "record",
38	  "next_action": "Review the remaining destination criterion.",
39	  "limitations": []
40	}
41	```
42	
43	`observed_at` is a caller-declared timezone-aware observation time no later than
44	recording; it is not generated viewing history. Each performed verdict references
45	one or more distinct observations of its required evidence mode (`local`, `visual`
46	or `live`). Unavailable verdicts have no observation indices and create no E.
47	Each supplied criterion must belong to this output. `supersedes` names its exact
48	current V or is null when none exists. Omitted criteria retain their current state.
49	Reasons, observations, next action and limitations remain specialist-authored.
50	An evidence file or schema alone cannot establish that the observation occurred.
51	
52	`action` is explicit: `record` retains judgments; `nominate` also selects this
53	candidate for its output, preserving other output selections; `complete` also
54	performs the existing task-completion checks/transitions. Completion needs every
55	output nominated and every required criterion passing, current allocation,
56	activation prerequisites and resolved pending jobs. A failed/unavailable review
57	is retained with record/nominate; asking to complete it fails before publication.
58	Already-done work must be explicitly reopened before a new review.
59	
60	The current canonical state hash protects publication. The semantic binding hash
61	protects the candidate, output/criteria and their complete semantic dependencies
62	even if a caller refreshes the state hash after a contract change. File SHA-256
63	values protect the observations. The adapter derives E scope, IDs and record
64	bindings; callers do not construct records or calculate a canonical state digest.
65	
66	## Retention, retries and limits
67	
68	Files are captured and copied under `STORE/reviews/<report-sha256>/`; the canonical
69	report contains the request, original paths, retained identities and source state.
70	Auxiliary X records bind retained files, and E binds the report plus candidate/Q
71	semantic scope. Report/file IDs are derived from REVIEW_ID. No supplied source
72	or previous evidence is overwritten. Maximum 64 observations, 64 MiB per file,
73	256 MiB aggregate and 1,024 declared verdicts; reports retain the codec size limit.
74	
75	The operation holds the store lock, checks the complete review/nomination/completion
76	sequence before publishing, then saves ordinary revisions. An interruption may
77	leave immutable unreferenced files or a retained review before completion. Reload
78	the current state hash and repeat the **same REVIEW_ID and observation** to finish;
79	existing review/verdict IDs are reused. Changed payloads, stale bindings or
80	superseded reviews cannot be replayed as new acceptance. A retry never submits a
81	provider job. Changing the review requires a new ID and explicit supersession.
82	
83	Results expose `state_hash` (canonical state), `review_sha256` (report file), current
84	criteria/nomination/task status and publication steps. Immutable snapshot creation
85	status stays separate from current acceptance. The report does not attest reviewer
86	identity, actual viewing or renderer honesty; retained host/runner evidence supplies
87	those observations. Generic source amendment and historical supersession retain
88	their existing PX2 semantics.
89	
90	## Save results directly
91	
92	Use CLI `--result-path work/review-result.json` or MCP `result_path` to save the
93	complete result without transcribing JSON, Windows paths or hashes. The option is
94	available for context, request-review, review-context, candidate-review, family,
95	family-snapshot and PLAR handoff. The path is relative to the explicit consumer
96	root and must be fresh; an existing destination is rejected before the operation.
97	The response contains `result_saved`, the path, file SHA-256, byte count and key
98	status fields. Read the saved file for complete criteria and publication details.
99	CLI full wire context remains PX text; other listed exports contain JSON.
100	
101	If writing fails after an operation publishes, the response has
102	`result_saved:false` and includes the actual `operation_result` (and `wire_result`
103	for wire context). CLI returns a nonzero exit code. Reconcile that result with
104	current state before retrying; a failed file export does not undo publication.
105	Use a fresh path and the operation's existing retry rules. Default output without
106	this option is unchanged; exports do not alter the saved-state format.

1	# Agent-to-agent asset work
2	
3	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
4	
5	## Caller → specialist
6	
7	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
8	
9	| Context | What the specialist needs |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
12	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
13	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
14	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
15	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
16	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
17	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
18	
19	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.
20	
21	For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.
22	
23	The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.
24	
25	When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
26	the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
27	criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
28	**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
29	scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
30	Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
31	A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
32	requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
33	also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
34	explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
35	Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.
36	
37	For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
38	when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
39	uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
40	Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
41	from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
42	assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
43	and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
44	claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.
45	
46	When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
47	critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
48	Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
49	message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
50	Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
51	caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
52	that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
53	child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
54	an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
55	foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
56	depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
57	changing the user's global configuration.
58	
59	A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.
60	
61	## Specialist → caller while working
62	
63	Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.
64	
65	Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.
66	
67	Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.
68	
69	Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.
70	
71	## Specialist → caller at completion
72	
73	Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
74	PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
75	of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
76	from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
77	without manufacturing PLAR or production records:
78	
79	- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
80	- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
81	- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
82	- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
83	- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
84	- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
85	- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.
86	
87	When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.
88	
89	Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.
90	
91	Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.
92	
93	The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.
94	
95	For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
96	use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`,
97	`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The
98	selected read's top-level `hash` identifies the PLAR file, not production state.
99	CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --path QUEUE --asset ID
100	--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --view caller --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
101	complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
102	Return the caller view and its exact handoff locator; the caller opens the retained
103	file and compares its state identity with fresh focused PLAR. Omitting `--view caller`
104	keeps the existing receipt response. The view does not add acceptance or alter the
105	saved handoff. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
106	Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
107	Before returning a reviewed open task, check its current nominee and workflow
108	requirements. Saved verdicts on an unselected candidate do not describe the
109	active output. Nominate the intended candidate through normal state authoring
110	when appropriate; preserve unavailable verdicts and leave the task open.
111	
112	`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
113	expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
114	caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
115	`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
116	runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
117	The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
118	does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.
119	
120	Use optional `details.caller` for the bounded ordinary return: summary, artifact
121	and report locators, issues and integration findings, following its closed
122	[contract](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md). Retain complete observations
123	in the other details fields and referenced files. Each declared file reference
124	contains exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`; the runtime verifies its current
125	confined file bytes before publishing. These checks do not verify the role or
126	judgment you supplied. The caller view distinguishes
127	these authored claims from derived task, acceptance and continuation facts.
128	A missing integration observation stays unreported; an accepted candidate does
129	not manufacture an assignment-status or integration claim. Without `details.caller`,
130	`caller.present` is false and the full details remain retrievable; legacy prose is
131	not automatically summarized.
132	
133	For example, only when the assigned destination inspection remains unperformed:
134	
135	```json
136	{
137	  "status": "partial",
138	  "caller": {
139	    "summary": "Candidate bytes are retained; required destination inspection remains unperformed.",
140	    "integration": {
141	      "status": "not_performed",
142	      "summary": "No destination observation has been made for this assignment."
143	    },
144	    "issues": [
145	      {
146	        "category": "unfinished_work",
147	        "summary": "The assigned destination check has not run.",
148	        "recovery": "Run the assigned destination check, retain its actual evidence and refresh the handoff."
149	      }
150	    ]
151	  }
152	}
153	```
154	
155	Use actual findings and omit inapplicable fields. Summary/recovery text is bounded
156	to 600 characters; artifact, report, issue and integration-evidence arrays each
157	hold at most 12 entries, and the complete caller block at most 8192 compact UTF-8
158	JSON bytes. Move detail to linked files instead of truncating obligations.
159	Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
160	`not_in_scope`; omission is not one of those observations.
161	
162	Follow the returned full-handoff, details and resume locators for exact retrieval.
163	Read `resume_inline`: the unchanged `resume` is present up to 4096 compact UTF-8
164	JSON bytes; otherwise `resume_ref` retrieves it in full. It is never rewritten or
165	truncated. `details_ref` and `resume_ref` identify physical source ranges and JSON
166	pointers in the same immutable handoff. Use its `path`/`sha256` for the full file.
167	These facts describe the captured selection; use the returned `refresh` read
168	after source or state changes, and reconcile the current identities. Read that full resume before acting on its jobs or
169	recovery instructions. Keep routine responses useful without pasting the complete
170	criteria audit, request report or tool transcript into the return.
171	
172	On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
173	requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
174	its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
175	actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
176	explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.
177	
178	Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.

1	# Preserve artistic requirement authority
2	
3	Read when translating an aesthetic brief into prompts, rejection criteria, or a review. The cases below document observed failure modes; their measured values are not universal pixel-art rules.
4	
5	For delegated work, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md) so the caller can inspect the actual artifacts independently. A self-audit is useful correction work, but its conclusion is not the caller's acceptance.
6	
7	Every production approach carries a compact authority table: property/value, requirement versus observation/proposal, exact source, and applicable scope. Carry the user's requested aesthetic into the derived prompts and checks. An image interpretation that differs from the brief is a reported uncertainty, not permission to replace that treatment. Only established project requirements become production rejection rules; proposals define labeled experiments. A measured color, gap, alpha level, component count or diagnostic contrast result remains an observation until adopted. Before the final handoff, reconcile every enforced restriction in the whole approach with that table; remove unsupported approval claims and keep diagnostic conclusions within their tested conditions.
8	
9	When the brief specifies a treatment, the proposed sample, production instructions and review criteria must all explicitly retain it. For requested selective anti-aliasing and partial transparency, describe where those treatments will be authored and how they will be reviewed; a reference interpretation such as “glow” does not replace either requirement. Uncertainty about a new shape calls for a treatment-preserving experiment, not a default ban on that shape or treatment. When no fixed palette is imposed, production checks omit exact palette membership; a palette experiment remains optional. Describe matching quality, lighting intent and provider reliability as interpretations or untested expectations unless evidence establishes them. A plan or a copied reference recipe cannot guarantee those outcomes.
10	
11	Test each derived restriction against a variation that still satisfies the brief. If that variation could fail the check, the extra restriction is a proposal, not an entailed requirement. Two detached antenna islands, for example, do not forbid another intentional detached detail or require the reference's total component count, coordinates or gap rows. Apply the same scope check to planned failure conclusions: one failed candidate establishes that attempt's failure, not a provider's general inability. A fallback can address that attempt without claiming a universal limit.
12	
13	After saving an approach, reopen and read the complete file before the final response. Audit the actual provider prompt, every proposed rejection check and every fallback conclusion against the authority table; reviewing the table or selected sections alone does not complete this step. For each added restriction, either identify its adopted source or label it as an optional experiment and remove it from production rejection rules. In a proposed experimental prompt, label the extra choices as proposals at the prompt itself. Correct contradictions such as an open alpha policy followed by an unexplained “no antialiasing” directive, or a qualitative color requirement turned into an invented numeric hue threshold. Preserve the earlier draft when revising it and report the scope and any unresolved conflict from this whole-file audit.
